subject: Procurement & approvals — Acme (PO vs card / marketplace / budget owner mapping)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement & approvals — Acme (PO vs card / marketplace / budget owner mapping)

Hi Tom / Lara —

Thanks again for the discovery call earlier today. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can map the internal approval path on your side: 

Recap:
- Acme is interested in a 90-day POC (hosted API) to validate recommendation quality and latency against production traffic.
- Primary use case: customer-facing semantic search + summarization (mid-size traffic).
- Key constraints: finance prefers PO for committed spend; security will need SOC2 evidence; legal has one standard addendum request.

Questions / asks (to help us qualify procurement readiness):
1) Preferred commercial path: card (self-serve) vs PO for the initial POC?
2) Marketplace interest: would transactable listing (AWS Marketplace) make procurement easier on your side?
3) Budget owner / economic buyer: who signs off on the spend (name + role)?
4) Finance sponsor & signatory path: who will raise PO / who signs the contract (procurement, finance, CFO)?

Attachments: procurement-checklist.pdf (short checklist we use to accelerate procurement reviews)

Next steps proposed:
- If you confirm the preferred commercial path (PO vs card) and the budget owner, we can provide a tailored quote and a minimal SOW.
- If PO, we can share our standard PO instructions and next steps for legal review.

Happy to hop on a quick 20-min sync with procurement / finance next week to walk through the process.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Schedule: https://calendly.com/marissa-cole/20min
From: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & approvals — Acme (PO vs card / marketplace / budget owner mapping)

Thanks Marissa — good summary. A few items from procurement/finance perspective: 

1) For anything above ~$25k total ARR we require a PO. For smaller pilots (under $5k) finance will allow a corporate card. The 90-day POC you mentioned will likely fall in the ~$10-30k band depending on token usage — so PO is the expected path.
2) Marketplace: yes, AWS Marketplace would help speed things up on our side (less paperwork). We do need the contract terms to be compatible with marketplace transactable listing.
3) Documents procurement will need: SOW (summary of services), W-9, standard insurance addendum, and a vendor form. I've attached a spreadsheet with our procurement questions for Redwood.
4) Budget owner / economic buyer: I'll be the technical sponsor, but final approval comes from Daniel Ruiz (VP Finance / signatory). CC'd procurement@acme.com who will own the PO.

Attaching: acme_procurement_questions.xlsx

Can you send the SOW + draft commercial terms and confirm whether Redwood is willing to accept PO for a POC and provide an invoice schedule? Also, if you have an AWS Marketplace listing ID we can share with our cloud procurement team.

-Tom
Tom O'Neill
Director, Machine Learning — Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & approvals — Acme (PO vs card / marketplace / budget owner mapping)

Appreciate the details, Tom — that's super helpful. tl;dr: we can absolutely accept a PO for the POC and support AWS Marketplace if you prefer that route. 

Answers / next steps: 
- Commercial path: PO is fine for the POC. For reference: POC estimate (90 days) ~ $18k (hosted API, expected token profile). We will provide an itemized SOW and monthly invoice schedule if you want to go PO.
- Marketplace: Redwood has an AWS Marketplace listing and can make the POC transactable; I will share the listing link and ID. Using the marketplace generally reduces procurement lead time but does require our listing to be used for the transaction.
- Docs we can provide immediately: short SOW, W-9, insurance cert, vendor form, and our procurement checklist (attached).

Vivek — looping you in to confirm the SOW template and whether legal needs anything additional for a marketplace listing. Also please confirm the signatory path for a PO vs card purchase so we can set the expectations for Daniel Ruiz and procurement.

Attachments: redwood-commercial-path.pdf

Tom / Lara — would you be open to a 20-min call with procurement + finance next Tues (Jun 8) to walk through the SOW and the PO process? If so I'll send a calendar invite and include the required docs ahead of time.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Lara Chen <lara.chen@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2026 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Procurement & approvals — Acme (PO vs card / marketplace / budget owner mapping)

Confirming internal mapping and recommended ask for the kickoff call: 

1) Economic buyer / technical sponsor: Tom O'Neill (Director, ML) — will validate technical success metrics and sign off on business value.
2) Finance sponsor: Lara Chen — will coordinate PO issuance and invoice routing.
3) Signatory path: final signatory is Daniel Ruiz (VP Finance) for agreements/committed spend > $25k. For the POC (~$18k) Daniel typically delegates sign-off to Finance Director (Lara) if there is an approved budget; otherwise Daniel signs. Procurement will issue PO.
4) Legal: minimal addendum expected — standard data processing and indemnity clauses. We'll circulate our standard SOW + marketplace-ready contract language.

Recommended next steps for the Tue Jun 8 call:
- Marissa to share SOW + invoice schedule + W-9 before the call.
- Acme procurement to confirm preferred purchasing path (PO via procurement or AWS Marketplace transactable).
- Confirm the name + contact of the person who will raise the PO and the expected timeline for issuance.

Marissa / Aditya — let me know if you want me to join the call and cover the SOW/marketplace framing. Happy to take the legal and product questions.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
